references.text: Moses encourages the Israelites not to fear the Egyptians because the Lord will fight for them, a theme repeated in Deuteronomy 20:1.
Joshua and Caleb urge the people not to fear the enemies in Canaan because the Lord is with them.
Joshua faces a great army with horses and chariots, but the Lord assures him of victory.
David declares that the Lord will grant victory against Goliath, regardless of the enemy's strength or weapons.
Elisha assures his servant that those who are with them are more than the enemy, despite the Syrians' horses and chariots.
Hezekiah encourages the people not to fear the Assyrian army because the Lord is with them.
Some trust in chariots and horses, but we call on the name of the Lord – this reflects confidence in God rather than military strength.
No king is saved by a large army, and the horse is unreliable for salvation – the Lord alone gives victory.
Woe to those who trust in Egypt's horses and chariots instead of seeking the Lord.
Do not fear, for I am with you – God's promise of presence as the basis for boldness.
If God is for us, who can be against us? This reflects confidence in God's presence in battle.
